resources.name: Agency on Aging of South Central Connecticut
resources.specificType: Regional Area Agency on Aging / Aging and Disability Resource Center: information and referral, CHOICES Medicare counseling, caregiver support, in-home assessment and case management
resources.address: 117 Washington Avenue, Suite 17, North Haven, CT 06473
resources.ages: Older adults, individuals with disabilities, and their caregivers
resources.hours: Contact for current office hours
resources.availability: Call and ask for 'Aging Answers' or service navigation to get started.
resources.cost: Free information, referral, and counseling services; some connected programs are income-based
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: The Agency on Aging of South Central Connecticut is the regional Area Agency on Aging serving Greater New Haven and the lower Naugatuck Valley, and it's often the best single starting point for a family that doesn't know where to begin. Information counselors help older adults and caregivers navigate state, federal, and community benefit programs, including free CHOICES counseling on Medicare options. The agency also offers caregiver-specific support: linking family caregivers to respite care, individual counseling, and training, plus in-home assessments and case management for programs like the Connecticut Home Care Program for Elders. Call and ask for 'Aging Answers' to get connected to a counselor rather than navigating the phone tree alone.

resources.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater New Haven (Columbus Clubhouse)
resources.specificType: K-8 afterschool, summer day camp, and teen/tween evening programming
resources.ages: K-8 for afterschool; ages 5-14 for summer camp; teen programs for high schoolers
resources.hours: Afterschool 2:30-6:00 PM, Mon-Fri during the school year; summer camp Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
resources.availability: Membership required. Contact for current enrollment status.
resources.cost: Membership-based; contact for current fees and financial assistance options
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater New Haven's Columbus Avenue Clubhouse, in the Hill neighborhood, runs afterschool programming from 2:30 to 6:00 PM on school days for kids in kindergarten through eighth grade, with bus service from most New Haven Public Schools directly to the Club. During the summer the Clubhouse shifts to a full-day camp model (roughly 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM) for children ages 5 to 14, which can cover the gap between when a school day ends and a parent's workday does. The Club also runs separate evening programming for middle and high schoolers, sports leagues, and a teen leadership track (Keystone Club) that includes college and career preparation.

resources.specificType: Preschool + Kitty Lustman-Findling Kindergarten
resources.hours: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM
resources.availability: Currently accepting applications for the 2026-2027 school year. Contact directly for current openings.
resources.cost: Sliding-scale tuition; priority enrollment for Yale faculty, staff, and student families, open to community families
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: Calvin Hill Day Care Center and the Kitty Lustman-Findling Kindergarten is a private, nonprofit preschool and kindergarten on Yale's campus in New Haven, serving both Yale-affiliated and community families. The program uses a progressive, integrated-day curriculum and is known for long-tenured teaching staff and active parent involvement, including a parent committee and one family work day per year. Tuition is offered on a sliding scale to keep the program accessible, and the center participates in the New Haven School Readiness Program. Priority enrollment goes to children of Yale faculty, staff, and students, but the program is open to families across the greater New Haven area.

resources.name: Common Ground High School, Urban Farm & Environmental Education Center
resources.specificType: Summer ecology day camp: Sprouts, Adventure, Treehouse, Amazing Animals, Cooking, and Rangers tracks, plus a Junior Counselor program
resources.ages: Ages 4-15 (Sprouts starts at 4; Junior Counselor track for 14+)
resources.hours: Camp day 8:30 AM - 3:00 PM, with extended day available until 5:30 PM
resources.availability: Registration opens late February for returning families, then general public; sessions often fill within days but a free waitlist is offered and spots regularly open as families' plans shift.
resources.cost: $655-$735 per two-week session depending on camp track (2026 pricing); financial aid available to qualified applicants from any town; over $30,000 awarded in camp scholarships annually
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: Common Ground's summer camp runs on a 20-acre urban farm at the base of West Rock Ridge State Park, with campers spending their days almost entirely outdoors: caring for farm animals, hiking, wading in the stream, building forts, and cooking over a campfire. Two-week sessions run late June through early August, with camp tracks organized by age and interest, including a dedicated Sprouts program for 4-to-6-year-olds and a cooking-focused camp. Extended day care is available until 5:30 PM for families who need coverage past the standard 3:00 PM pickup. Making camp financially accessible is core to the program's mission: Common Ground provides over $30,000 in scholarships each summer and actively works to reach underserved New Haven neighborhoods and schools.

resources.name: Neighborhood Music School
resources.specificType: Summer music, dance, and drama programs; also a state-certified preschool and year-round instruction
resources.ages: 6 months to 80+ years-round; summer camp programs mainly school-age
resources.hours: Mon-Fri 8:15 AM-9:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, Sun 11:00 AM-5:00 PM (school hours; specific camp/class times vary)
resources.availability: Contact for current summer program schedule and openings.
resources.cost: About 15% of students receive financial aid or scholarship assistance; contact for current tuition
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: Neighborhood Music School is one of the largest community arts schools in the country, teaching more than 30 instruments and seven genres of dance out of its Audubon Arts District campus a short walk from Yale's central campus. Alongside year-round private lessons, ensembles, and a state-certified preschool, NMS runs summer programs in rock, jazz, and other musical genres where kids build performance skills, learn recording basics, and play alongside other musicians. About 15 percent of the school's roughly 3,000 annual students receive financial aid or scholarship support, and the school serves ages from 6 months through adulthood, so it can be a long-term home for a family rather than a single-summer stop.

resources.specificType: Infant through pre-kindergarten, plus part-time and short-term care options
resources.hours: Monday-Friday, 7:30 AM - 5:30 PM
resources.availability: Part-time (2-3 days/week) and short-term care (1 day to 8 weeks) sometimes available. Contact directly for current infant waitlist status.
resources.cost: Contact center for current tuition; scholarship application available
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: The Phyllis Bodel Childcare Center at Yale School of Medicine cares for children from six weeks through pre-kindergarten in a licensed center near the medical school campus. Teachers work full days, five days a week, so children are not shifted between staff during the day, and the center stays open in inclement weather to support parents' work schedules. Beyond full-time care, Phyllis Bodel offers part-time slots (two or three days a week) and occasional short-term care ranging from one day to eight weeks, which can help families bridging a gap in coverage. The center is affiliated with the Yale School of Medicine and is open to families from the broader New Haven community, not just Yale affiliates.

resources.notes: Right at Home of New Haven County is a locally owned, licensed non-medical home care agency (Connecticut DCP Registration #HCA.0000342) based in Milford and serving New Haven, Hamden, North Haven, and the surrounding towns. Caregivers provide companionship, help with errands and medical appointments, light housekeeping, and personal care such as bathing and dressing, with care available around the clock even though the office itself keeps standard business hours. The New Haven County office won Home Care Pulse's 2026 Best of Home Care Provider of Choice and Employer of Choice awards. A complimentary custom service plan consultation is the usual starting point for a family figuring out what level of help they actually need.

resources.name: The Connecticut Hospice
resources.specificType: Inpatient hospital plus home-based hospice/palliative care, skilled home care, Magnolia dementia care program, and respite care
resources.ages: Adult and pediatric hospice patients (dedicated pediatric home hospice program)
resources.hours: Intake and inpatient facility open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; administrative offices Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
resources.availability: Admissions department reachable 24/7. Contact intake directly to discuss timing.
resources.cost: Covered by Medicare, Medicaid, and most private insurance for eligible hospice care; as a non-profit, additional services are supported by donations
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: The Connecticut Hospice in Branford was the first hospice in the United States and remains the only one in the state with its own dedicated inpatient hospital, a waterfront facility overlooking Long Island Sound. It offers both inpatient and home-based hospice and palliative care, along with skilled home care, a dementia-focused Magnolia Care program, and short-term respite care (up to five days) for family caregivers who need a break. The centralized intake department takes calls 24 hours a day, seven days a week, which matters for families making end-of-life decisions on short notice. As a non-profit, the organization also relies on donor support to cover services and therapies not fully reimbursed by insurance.

resources.name: Whitney Center
resources.specificType: Continuing Care/Life Plan community: independent living, assisted living, memory care (Meadow Mills), and skilled nursing on one campus
resources.ages: Adults 55+ for independent living; assisted living, memory care, and skilled nursing residents typically older
resources.hours: Marketing & Sales office Mon-Fri 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; residence staffed 24/7
resources.availability: Contact for current waitlist and unit availability by care level.
resources.cost: Contact for current pricing; entrance-fee Life Care model is designed so costs typically don't spike if a resident's care needs increase over time
resources.contact: (203) 974-0001 Marketing & Sales | (203) 281-6745 Main | (203) 848-2222 Memory Care (Meadow Mills)
resources.submittedBy: Village Notes team (public listing, not yet reviewed by a parent/caregiver)
resources.notes: Whitney Center is a non-profit Life Plan (continuing care) community in Hamden that lets residents move between independent living, assisted living, memory care, and skilled nursing on the same campus as their needs change, without relocating to a new facility each time. Its memory care neighborhood, Meadow Mills, is a secured unit designed specifically for residents who need memory support, with staff and structured activities built around that population. Because it's a Life Care community, the entrance-fee model is designed so a resident's costs don't spike if they need a higher level of care later, one of the bigger financial unknowns families run into with elder care. The campus includes amenities like a fitness center, pool, art studio, and cultural arts center, and it serves the Greater New Haven area specifically.
